solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Duke has possession of hills

parts.note: to have possession of something is to own it, so this gives owns

explanation.surface: A nobleman holds title to a stretch of hilly land.
explanation.definitionFit: Downs are rolling chalk uplands in southern England, such as the South Downs, so the word is a synonym for hills.

clue.text: Merit of French verse, translated

parts.note: de is the French word for of

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters are converted into another form, here rearranged

explanation.surface: A judgment on whether a French poem, once rendered into English, is any good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' seems to continue the French theme, but it is the signal to rearrange the poem's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to have earned it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Order new car and old wine for glass worker

indicators.note: to order letters is to put them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy a fresh car and vintage wine, oddly addressed to someone who works with glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges the letters of NEW CAR and OLD WINE together; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cleans panes for a living works on glass, a playful description of the trade.

clue.text: Preach of dreadful mores in South East

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something in a terrible state, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for South East

explanation.surface: Someone lecturing about the awful morals of south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges MORES IN together with SE; the S and E end up at either end of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To sermonise is to deliver a moralising lecture, a synonym of preach in its moralising sense.

clue.text: Rest day brings Southern seaman to city

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor
Bath is a historic city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: A sailor from the south heads into town on his day off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest observed in Judaism and Christianity.

clue.text: One criticising roof worker

definitions.meaning: to slate is British informal for to criticise harshly, so one who does so
a tradesman who covers roofs with slates

explanation.definitionFit: Slate means to criticise severely, and a tradesman laying slates on roofs bears the same name.

clue.text: Stole unfinished vessel

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a boat is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone took an incomplete pot or ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as a verb but is the noun: a scarf-like wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long feathery or fur scarf, a kind of stole worn round the shoulders.

clue.text: Aura, iron, that I represented as strict

indicators.note: represented as suggests the letters are shown in a different form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of odd words being presented as something severe.
explanation.definitionFit: An authoritarian regime or person demands strict obedience, so the adjective matches strict.

clue.text: Difficult — that endless road

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its letters at both ends

explanation.surface: A complaint that a road which never ends is a tough one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and difficult are straightforward synonyms describing a demanding task.

clue.text: Informed attitude about drink

parts.note: to sing is slang for to inform on someone, so informed gives sang

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word around

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: A knowing stance on what to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Informed' looks like an adjective meaning knowledgeable but is the past tense of grassing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Take front off roof beam at later time

indicators.note: taking the front off means removing the first letter

parts.note: a rafter is a sloping beam supporting a roof

explanation.surface: A builder's instruction to remove the end of a beam later on.
explanation.definitionFit: After as an adverb means subsequently, at a time later than something else.

clue.text: Greek character don droned on about shrub

parts.note: rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A university teacher bored everyone talking about a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DON DRONED into DODENDRON; 'on' only links. A don is a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhododendron is a flowering evergreen bush, an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Drug upset unfashionable, hot US area

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
something out is no longer in fashion
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A drug that is passé and spicy disturbs someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deep South is the region of the southern United States including Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi.

clue.text: Old mathematician returning snooker equipment cover

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cue is the stick used in snooker
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: An elderly maths teacher brings back the cover for snooker gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek mathematician known as the father of geometry.

clue.text: Small and attractive — favourite item Monsiieur's missed

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: missed means that letter is left out of the word

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman fails to notice a dainty, pretty and much-loved object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monsiieur' is a typo for Monsieur in the clue as published.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite describes a woman who is slight and dainty, so small and attractive.

clue.text: Ensure observance of education extremely supportive of church

indicators.note: extremely means take the letters at the extremes, first and last

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A school's teaching is strongly supportive of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a rule is to compel compliance with it, ensuring it is observed.

clue.text: Tripper familiar with Charleston perhaps

definitions.meaning: one who trips the light fantastic, an old phrase for dancing
someone who knows a 1920s step such as the Charleston

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripper' suggests a tourist or someone who stumbles, and Charleston a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dances trips lightly on their feet and might know the Charleston, a 1920s ballroom step.

clue.text: Widespread stick for top officers

parts.note: general means widespread, as in general opinion
a staff is a walking stick

explanation.surface: A walking stick is in common use among the senior ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The general staff are the senior officers who assist a commander in planning operations.

clue.text: Regularly perform in concert

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone frequently plays at live shows.
explanation.walkthrough: A Prom is one of the BBC Promenade concerts held each summer in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for promenade concert, a prom is a concert where some of the audience stand.

clue.text: Add life to routine, English not exaclty working initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Advice to liven up a dull English habit that is not quite functioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exaclty' is a typo for exactly in the clue as published; its first letter is unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to revive it or give it fresh vigour.

clue.text: Got Korean money

definitions.meaning: past tense meaning obtained or gained, as a prize is gained
the currency unit of North and South Korea

explanation.definitionFit: Won is the past tense of win, meaning got, and also the Korean currency.

clue.text: Messenger in firm, curt ignoring outsiders? That's right

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: ignoring outsiders means dropping the first and last letters

parts.note: ie, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A company's go-between is brusque, though not entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier delivers packages or messages, so is a kind of messenger.

clue.text: Pit worker welcomes a Republican sailor

indicators.note: welcomes means the first piece takes the others in

parts.note: a miner works in a coal pit

explanation.surface: A coal miner greets a Republican sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, an old-fashioned synonym for sailor.

clue.text: Movable mechanism from Munich in Germany

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A piece of machinery sourced from a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the jointed device on which a door or lid swings, a moving mechanism.
